what: bench/prune_bench: 1M finished jobs (3M dedup hashes, 509 MB) spread over 60 days; prune everything older than 30 days while a second connection commits one row every 2 ms
machine: same dev VM as the other results, Postgres 16 local, default config
takeaway: Pruning half a million jobs takes under 4 s and adds about 0.4 ms to concurrent commit p99. Batch size makes no measurable latency difference here, because the deleted rows are old finished jobs nothing else touches; batches are kept for bounded transactions (a failure or shutdown loses at most one batch of work, and WAL per transaction stays small).
